name: Office core 2: working life
description: A second set of 100 words for anyone in any office role: writing, time, meetings, careers, pay, business basics and conduct.

cards.subject: proofreading
says: is reading a finished piece of writing to catch spelling, grammar and typing mistakes
is done after the content is settled
cards.use: have finished a letter and want to catch typing slips before it goes out
not: is the stage where the main argument is first drafted

cards.subject: editing
says: improves the content, structure and clarity of a piece of writing
may cut, reorder or rewrite whole passages
cards.use: find that a report is correct but long-winded and badly ordered
not: only checks spelling and punctuation

cards.subject: plain English
says: uses short, familiar words and clear sentences so that readers understand first time
avoids unnecessary jargon
cards.use: are writing to people who are not specialists
not: means leaving out important detail

cards.subject: jargon
says: is specialist vocabulary understood by people inside a field but not by outsiders
can make writing hard for a general reader
cards.use: notice a letter to the public is full of terms only your team uses
not: is always wrong to use in any document

cards.subject: acronym
says: is a short form made from the first letters of a longer name
should be spelled out in full the first time it is used
cards.use: want to shorten a long title but readers may not know it
not: is a word that has the opposite meaning of another

cards.subject: executive summary
says: is a short section at the start of a long document that gives the main findings and recommendation
lets a busy reader decide without reading everything
cards.use: have a forty-page report and a director who has two minutes
not: is a detailed appendix of every source used

cards.subject: house style
says: is an organisation's own rules for spelling, layout, tone and formatting
keeps documents from different authors looking consistent
cards.use: need all the team's documents to use the same conventions
not: is the layout of the office building

cards.subject: tone of voice
says: is the attitude a piece of writing conveys, such as formal, friendly or firm
should suit the reader and the purpose
cards.use: are writing a reply to an upset customer and must sound calm and respectful
not: is the volume of someone's speaking voice

cards.subject: brief
says: is a short written instruction that says what is wanted, why and by when
gives someone enough to start work
cards.use: are handing a task to a colleague and want them to know the purpose and deadline
not: is a long final report after the work is done

cards.subject: boilerplate
says: is standard text reused unchanged in many documents
often covers things like company descriptions or legal wording
cards.use: have a paragraph about the company that appears at the end of every press release
not: is a first rough draft that will be rewritten

cards.subject: time management
says: is planning how to spend your hours so the important work gets done
includes deciding what to do first and what to leave
cards.use: keep running out of time before the key task is finished
not: means working longer hours every day

cards.subject: to-do list
says: is a written list of tasks that still need doing
can be ordered by priority or by date
cards.use: have many small jobs and are afraid of forgetting one
not: is a record of tasks already completed

cards.subject: time blocking
says: sets aside chosen blocks of the day for specific tasks
protects focused time in a diary
cards.use: want two uninterrupted hours for a report and mark them in your calendar
not: means taking a long break between meetings

cards.subject: buffer time
says: is spare time left between tasks or meetings to absorb overruns
stops one delay from knocking out the rest of the day
cards.use: have back-to-back meetings that regularly overrun
not: is the time a task is expected to take

cards.subject: urgent versus important
says: separates what must be done soon from what matters most for goals
warns that urgent tasks can crowd out important ones
cards.use: spend every day answering messages while a key project stalls
not: means the two always describe the same task

cards.subject: interruption
says: is anything that breaks your concentration on a task
can cost time getting back into the work
cards.use: cannot finish a task because people keep stopping at your desk
not: is a planned break scheduled in the diary

cards.subject: delegation
says: is giving a task to someone else while staying accountable for the result
needs a clear brief and the authority to do the job
cards.use: have more work than you can do and a capable colleague with spare time
not: is passing a problem on so that you no longer have any responsibility for it

cards.subject: batching
says: is doing similar small tasks together in one session
reduces the cost of switching between kinds of work
cards.use: find that checking email all day stops you concentrating, so you check at set times
not: is spreading the same task thinly across the whole week

cards.subject: diary management
says: is keeping a calendar accurate and organised for yourself or someone else
includes arranging, moving and declining meetings
cards.use: are asked to arrange a director's meetings for the week
not: is writing a personal journal at home

cards.subject: chair
says: leads a meeting, keeps to the agenda and makes sure everyone can speak
keeps the discussion moving to a decision
cards.use: are running a meeting where two people keep talking over each other
not: writes the minutes while the meeting happens

cards.subject: facilitator
says: guides a group's discussion without pushing their own view
helps a group reach its own conclusion
cards.use: are leading a workshop and want everyone's ideas heard fairly
not: decides alone what the group will do

cards.subject: note-taker
says: records the main points and actions while a meeting runs
may write the formal minutes afterwards
cards.use: need someone to capture the actions at today's meeting
not: leads the discussion and sets the agenda

cards.subject: agenda item
says: is a single topic listed to be covered in a meeting
often has a lead person and a time allowance
cards.use: want to add a budget question to the next team meeting
not: is a task given to a person at the end of a meeting

cards.subject: parking lot
says: is a place to record off-topic points so that they can be dealt with later
keeps a meeting on the agenda without losing good ideas
cards.use: find a useful but unrelated issue is derailing the meeting
not: is a list of the decisions the meeting has made

cards.subject: consensus
says: is general agreement that a group can accept even if not everyone's first choice
is reached by discussion rather than a vote
cards.use: want a team to commit to a plan that everyone can live with
not: means every person agrees completely with every detail

cards.subject: majority vote
says: decides an issue by what most voters choose
settles a question even when some people disagree
cards.use: have a committee split on a proposal and need a decision at the meeting
not: only passes if everyone votes yes

cards.subject: ground rules
says: are agreed ways a group will behave in a meeting or workshop
might include listening without interrupting and keeping to time
cards.use: are starting a new project group and want to agree how it will work
not: are the legal rules a company must obey

cards.subject: hybrid meeting
says: has some people in a room and others joining online
needs the online people to be able to see and hear properly
cards.use: have half the team in the office and half at home
not: is a meeting held entirely over a phone line

cards.subject: recap
says: is a short summary of what has been said or agreed
is often given at the end of a meeting to confirm actions
cards.use: want to check that everyone leaves knowing who does what
not: is the agenda circulated before the meeting

cards.subject: sponsor
says: is a senior person who backs a project and removes obstacles for it
holds the budget or authority the project depends on
cards.use: need senior support to get a project's funding approved
not: is the person who does the daily work on the project

cards.subject: teamwork
says: is people working together towards a shared goal
relies on trust and clear roles
cards.use: are asked how your group will finish the project together
not: is each person completing their own work with no contact

cards.subject: collaboration
says: is people actively creating or solving something together
often uses shared documents and joint discussion
cards.use: are co-writing a proposal with a colleague in another department
not: means one person doing the task while others watch

cards.subject: accountability
says: means being answerable for the outcome of a task or decision
stays with a person even when others help
cards.use: must explain to the director why the deadline was missed
not: is the same as blaming a team member

cards.subject: responsibility
says: is the duty to carry out a task or look after something
can be shared among several people
cards.use: are given charge of arranging the team's training
not: is the final answer to a regulator or board for a result

cards.subject: point of contact
says: is the named person others should go to about a matter
spares people from having to find the right colleague
cards.use: need to give a client one person to call about their order
not: is the place where two roads meet

cards.subject: buddy
says: is a colleague who helps a new starter settle in informally
answers everyday questions that a manager may not have time for
cards.use: are starting a new job and want a friendly person to ask where things are
not: is the person who conducts your appraisal

cards.subject: negotiation
says: is discussion between two sides to reach an agreement
aims for terms both sides can accept
cards.use: need to agree a price and delivery date with a supplier
not: is demanding that the other side accepts your first offer

cards.subject: networking
says: is building and keeping useful professional relationships
opens routes to advice, jobs and information
cards.use: want to meet people in other organisations who do similar work
not: means sending the same mass message to everyone you know

cards.subject: training course
says: is a planned session or programme that teaches a skill
can be run in person or online
cards.use: need to learn how to use a new system
not: is a formal review of someone's performance

cards.subject: CPD
says: is continuing professional development: learning kept up throughout a career
is often recorded to keep a professional status
cards.use: must show your professional body that you have kept your knowledge current
not: is a one-off exam taken only when joining a profession

cards.subject: qualification
says: is formal proof, such as a certificate or degree, that someone has reached a standard
is awarded after assessment
cards.use: want a recognised award that shows you have passed a recognised test
not: is a short note of thanks from a manager

cards.subject: apprenticeship
says: combines paid work with structured training towards a qualification
lets someone learn on the job
cards.use: are offered a job in which you work four days and study one
not: is an unpaid week of watching colleagues

cards.subject: secondment
says: is a temporary move to another team or organisation
returns the person to their original job afterwards
cards.use: are offered six months in another department to gain experience, then to come back
not: is a permanent transfer to a new employer

cards.subject: promotion
says: moves an employee into a more senior role
usually brings more responsibility and often more pay
cards.use: have taken on more responsibility and are made team leader
not: is moving to a role at the same level in another team

cards.subject: lateral move
says: is a move to a different role at the same level
builds new skills without a rise in grade
cards.use: want experience in another function without a change of grade
not: is a step up to a higher grade

cards.subject: reference
says: is a statement from a former employer or other person about someone's suitability
is requested by an employer considering a hire
cards.use: are asked by a new employer for a former manager's opinion of you
not: is the list of sources at the end of a report

cards.subject: resignation
says: is when an employee formally chooses to leave their job
is normally given in writing
cards.use: have decided to leave and must tell your employer
not: is when an employer ends a person's job

cards.subject: redundancy
says: is when a job ends because the work is no longer needed
is not a judgement of the person's performance
cards.use: are told your role is being closed because the department is shrinking
not: is the same as being dismissed for poor work

cards.subject: salary
says: is a fixed yearly amount paid to an employee in regular instalments
does not change with the hours worked in a month
cards.use: are offered a job paying a set amount a year
not: is pay calculated hour by hour

cards.subject: wage
says: is pay calculated for the hours worked
may change from week to week
cards.use: are paid for each hour you work and your pay differs each week
not: is a fixed yearly amount that never varies

cards.subject: gross pay
says: is pay before tax and other deductions
is the headline figure agreed for the job
cards.use: want to know the amount agreed before anything is taken off
not: is the amount that reaches your bank account

cards.subject: net pay
says: is pay after tax and other deductions have been taken off
is the amount received in the bank
cards.use: want to know how much will be paid into your account
not: is the pay promised before deductions

cards.subject: pension
says: is money put aside during working life to provide an income in retirement
may be paid into by both employee and employer
cards.use: want to know how a workplace scheme will provide for you later in life
not: is a payment made to cover health costs while working

cards.subject: bonus
says: is an extra payment on top of normal pay
may depend on performance or results
cards.use: are paid an extra sum for meeting a yearly target
not: is the fixed pay you receive every month

cards.subject: commission
says: is pay calculated as a share of the sales a person makes
rises as sales rise
cards.use: are a sales person paid a percentage of each deal you close
not: is a fixed monthly sum regardless of sales

cards.subject: employee benefits
says: are rewards beyond pay, such as private healthcare or extra leave
may be part of the package offered by an employer
cards.use: are comparing two job offers and one includes health cover
not: are only the wages for overtime

cards.subject: pay review
says: is a regular check of whether employees' pay should change
may be linked to inflation, performance or the market
cards.use: want to know when your employer will next consider changing salaries
not: is an examination to confirm tax has been paid

cards.subject: profit
says: is what is left after costs are taken from income
shows whether a business makes more than it spends
cards.use: want to know whether the business earned more than it spent
not: is all the money a business receives from sales

cards.subject: loss
says: is the result when costs are higher than income
means a business has spent more than it earned
cards.use: find that the year's costs were larger than its income
not: is the money left after all costs are paid

cards.subject: overhead
says: is a running cost not tied to one product, such as rent or utilities
has to be paid whether or not sales rise
cards.use: want to count the cost of the building and electricity
not: is the direct cost of materials in a product

cards.subject: turnover
says: is the total value of sales over a period
is measured before costs are taken off
cards.use: want the total value of everything sold last year
not: is the number of staff who leave in a year

cards.subject: head office
says: is the main site from which an organisation is directed
often houses senior management
cards.use: are told that the company's top decisions are made at its main location
not: is a small local site that serves customers

cards.subject: subsidiary
says: is a company owned or controlled by a larger parent company
is a separate legal entity
cards.use: learn that a firm is wholly owned by another but trades under its own name
not: is a department with no separate legal existence

cards.subject: board of directors
says: is the group that oversees a company and sets its direction
appoints the chief executive
cards.use: want to know who holds the chief executive to account
not: is the team that handles the day-to-day tasks

cards.subject: chief executive
says: is the most senior manager responsible for running an organisation day to day
reports to the board
cards.use: want to know who has overall charge of the organisation's operations
not: is the person who owns all of the company's shares

cards.subject: shareholder
says: is a person or organisation that owns shares in a company
may vote on key company matters
cards.use: own part of a company by holding its shares
not: is any person affected by a company's actions

cards.subject: public sector
says: is the part of the economy run by government and funded mainly by taxes
includes services like state schools and the civil service
cards.use: work for a body that is owned and funded by the state
not: is made up of privately owned companies

cards.subject: private sector
says: is the part of the economy made up of privately owned businesses
aims to make a profit for its owners
cards.use: work for a company owned by individuals or shareholders
not: is run directly by the government

cards.subject: organisation chart
says: is a diagram showing the structure of an organisation and who reports to whom
helps new staff find the right person
cards.use: need to see who your manager's manager is
not: is a chart of the organisation's yearly profits

cards.subject: enquiry
says: is a question from a person or business about a product or service
may lead to a sale
cards.use: get a message asking what you charge for a service
not: is a formal complaint about poor work

cards.subject: lead
says: is a person or organisation that might become a customer
is followed up by the sales team
cards.use: collect the contact details of a visitor who asked for a demonstration
not: is a customer who has already bought and left

cards.subject: sales pipeline
says: shows the stages that sales opportunities pass through
helps forecast future sales
cards.use: want to see how many deals are at each stage
not: is a list of products in stock

cards.subject: upsell
says: offers an existing customer a more expensive or fuller version
aims to raise the value of a sale
cards.use: suggest that a customer buying a basic plan take the premium plan
not: is selling the same item at a discount

cards.subject: refund
says: is money returned to a customer for something they paid for
is given when goods are returned or a service fails
cards.use: are returning faulty goods and want your money back
not: is a discount offered before the purchase

cards.subject: warranty
says: is a promise from a seller to repair or replace a faulty product for a set period
covers faults rather than misuse
cards.use: find your new laptop stopped working after two months
not: is a promise to deliver by a stated date

cards.subject: terms and conditions
says: are the rules that set out the agreement between a business and its customer
cover things like payment, returns and liability
cards.use: are about to buy and want to know the rules that apply
not: are the list of the product's features

cards.subject: turnaround time
says: is the time between receiving a request and completing it
is often set as a target for a service
cards.use: want to know how long the team takes to process an order
not: is the time a customer spends choosing a product

cards.subject: customer satisfaction
says: measures how happy customers are with a product or service
is often gathered with surveys
cards.use: send a short survey after each order to see whether people are pleased
not: is the number of customers a business has

cards.subject: brand
says: is the identity, reputation and promise people link to an organisation
includes its name, look and tone
cards.use: want to explain what makes a company recognisable and trusted
not: is the physical product that is sold

cards.subject: cloud storage
says: keeps files on internet-connected servers so they can be reached from many devices
lets people share files without sending copies
cards.use: want to open the same file from your laptop and your phone
not: is storage that only works on one computer

cards.subject: video call
says: is a meeting where participants see and hear each other over the internet
needs a camera, microphone and connection
cards.use: want to speak face to face with a colleague in another city
not: is a phone call that only carries sound

cards.subject: chat channel
says: is a shared space for messages on one topic or team
lets many people read and reply in one place
cards.use: want quick team discussion that does not clog email
not: is a private note that only one person can see

cards.subject: screen sharing
says: lets others on a call see what is on your screen
is used to demonstrate or explain something
cards.use: want to walk a colleague through a document while on a call
not: sends your files to the others on the call

cards.subject: shared calendar
says: lets several people see each other's availability
makes it easier to find a time for a meeting
cards.use: want to see when four colleagues are all free
not: is a list of public holidays printed on paper

cards.subject: PDF
says: is a file format that keeps a document's layout the same on any device
is hard to edit without special tools
cards.use: want to send a final document that will look the same for everyone
not: is a type of spreadsheet used for calculations

cards.subject: file format
says: is the way data is arranged in a file and shown by its extension
decides which programs can open the file
cards.use: cannot open a file because your software does not support its type
not: is the name you give a file

cards.subject: mailing list
says: is a group of email addresses that can be sent a message at once
lets one message reach all subscribers
cards.use: want to send a newsletter to all your members
not: is a printed list of postal addresses only

cards.subject: password manager
says: stores strong, unique passwords securely so that you need remember only one
can fill them in on websites
cards.use: have dozens of accounts and keep reusing the same weak password
not: is a rule that says how often a password must be typed

cards.subject: software update
says: is a new version of a program that fixes problems or adds features
often includes security fixes
cards.use: see a message that a newer version of your tools is ready
not: is a request to buy extra licences

cards.subject: code of conduct
says: is a set of rules on how people in an organisation must behave
applies to everyone in the organisation
cards.use: want to check what behaviour your employer expects of you
not: is a list of the products a company sells

cards.subject: equal opportunities
says: means giving everyone a fair chance whatever their background
applies to hiring, training and promotion
cards.use: want to make sure the recruitment process treats every candidate fairly
not: means everyone must receive identical pay

cards.subject: discrimination
says: is treating a person worse because of a protected characteristic such as race or sex
is unlawful in most workplaces
cards.use: see a person turned down for a job because of their age
not: is choosing the best candidate for a job on merit

cards.subject: harassment
says: is unwanted behaviour that offends, intimidates or humiliates someone
can happen in person or online
cards.use: find that a colleague keeps making offensive remarks about someone
not: is a fair complaint raised through the proper channel

cards.subject: non-disclosure agreement
says: is a contract promising to keep certain information secret
can bind both individuals and companies
cards.use: are about to share an unreleased plan with a partner and want it kept private
not: is a promise to deliver work by a date

cards.subject: gifts and hospitality
says: are offers from outside people that must be declared or refused under policy
can be seen as an attempt to influence decisions
cards.use: are offered tickets to an event by a supplier you are about to choose
not: are items that your employer gives you on your birthday

cards.subject: copyright
says: gives the creator of an original work the right to control copying it
applies to text, images, music and software
cards.use: want to know whether you can reuse someone's photograph in a leaflet
not: protects ideas that have not been written or recorded

cards.subject: fraud
says: is deliberately deceiving someone to gain money or an advantage
includes false expense claims
cards.use: find a colleague has invented receipts to claim money
not: is a genuine mistake in a calculation

cards.subject: tax
says: is money collected by the government from earnings and purchases
is often taken from pay before it reaches the employee
cards.use: want to know why your net pay is smaller than your gross pay
not: is a voluntary gift an employer adds to pay

cards.subject: insurance
says: pays out money if a covered loss happens, in return for regular payments
spreads the cost of unlikely but costly events
cards.use: want protection against the cost of a fire at your premises
not: guarantees that a business will make a profit

cards.subject: annual report
says: is a yearly document describing an organisation's activities and finances
is published for owners and other readers
cards.use: want to see how the organisation performed over the whole year
not: is a monthly list of staff who joined

cards.subject: fiduciary duty
says: is a legal duty to act in the best interests of another party
applies to people such as company directors and trustees
cards.use: are a director and must put the company's interests ahead of your own
not: is a duty to keep an office tidy

qa.q: Which task checks a finished letter for spelling and typing slips?
qa.why: Proofreading catches mistakes in finished writing.

qa.q: A letter to the public is full of terms only your team understands. What is this problem?
qa.why: Jargon is specialist vocabulary outsiders do not know.

qa.q: What does the first use of an acronym in a document normally need?
wrong: A footnote with the author's name
qa.why: Spell it out first so every reader understands.

qa.q: Which pay is calculated for each hour worked?
qa.why: A wage depends on the hours worked.

qa.q: Which statement shows how gross pay and deductions led to net pay?
qa.why: A payslip breaks down a payment.

qa.q: Who should a client contact about their order if you give them one named person?
qa.why: A point of contact is the named person to go to.

qa.q: A director has two minutes and a forty-page report. What do you give them?
qa.why: It gives the main findings and recommendation up front.

qa.q: A report has correct facts but is long and badly ordered. What does it need?
qa.why: Editing improves the content and structure, not only the typing.

qa.q: You earn £30,000 a year before tax. What is that figure?
qa.why: Gross pay is before deductions.

qa.q: Which figure is the amount that actually reaches your bank?
qa.why: Net pay is after tax and deductions.

qa.q: A meeting keeps being derailed by an off-topic issue that is still useful. What helps?
qa.why: Park the point to deal with later.

qa.q: Some of a team are in the office and some at home for one meeting. What is it?
qa.why: Part of the group is in the room and part online.

qa.q: A company wants to know how much of its sales were left after the product cost. Which figure?
qa.why: Gross margin is sales less the direct cost of goods.

qa.q: A firm is profitable but cannot pay bills because customers pay late. What is the problem?
qa.why: Money arrives later than it must go out.

qa.q: Which person leads a meeting and keeps it to the agenda?
qa.why: The chair keeps the meeting on track.

qa.q: Two people keep interrupting each other in a meeting you are running. What fits first?
wrong: Hold a vote on who is right
qa.why: Ground rules set how the group behaves.

qa.q: You are asked to choose a supplier run by your brother. What should you do?
wrong: Ask the supplier to hide it
qa.why: Declare it so someone else can decide.

qa.q: A supplier offers you event tickets just before you choose between suppliers. What do you do?
qa.right: Decline or declare under the gifts policy
wrong: Accept and give a better score
qa.why: It could look like an attempt to influence your choice.

qa.q: A colleague tells you of falsified safety records. What is the safe route?
qa.why: Report serious wrongdoing to someone who can act.

qa.q: A manager assigns a task but keeps the final answer to the director for it. What is this?
qa.why: The task is delegated but accountability stays.

qa.q: A report, a speech and a leaflet all start with the same standard paragraph about the company. What is it?
qa.why: Standard text reused unchanged.

qa.q: Many small tasks stop you concentrating all day. What helps?
qa.why: Batching cuts the cost of switching.

qa.q: A person's pay is a share of each deal they close. What is that?
qa.why: Commission rises with sales.

qa.q: You see urgent tasks crowding out a key project. Which idea helps?
qa.why: Urgent is not always important.

qa.q: A new person wants help with everyday questions. Who suits that role best?
qa.why: A buddy helps a new starter informally.

qa.q: You are comparing two job offers. One includes private healthcare. What is that?
qa.why: Benefits are rewards beyond pay.

qa.q: You want a long meeting to leave with a clear plan. What should the chair do at the end?
qa.right: Give a recap of the actions
qa.why: A recap confirms who does what.

qa.q: A project needs a senior person to remove obstacles and secure funding. Who?
qa.why: The sponsor backs the project with authority and budget.

qa.q: You want to see how many sales deals are at each stage so you can forecast. What shows this?
qa.why: A pipeline shows the stages deals pass through.

qa.q: A staff member is moved temporarily to another team for six months and then returns. What is this?
qa.why: A secondment is temporary and returns the person.

qa.q: A van bought for the business loses value each year. What is this reduction called?
qa.why: Depreciation spreads the fall in an asset's value.

qa.q: A role closes because the work is no longer needed, not because of the person. What is this?
qa.why: Redundancy is about the job, not performance.

qa.q: A group has a plan that not everyone loves but everyone can accept. What was reached?
qa.why: Consensus is a position everyone can live with.

qa.q: You are about to share an unreleased plan with a partner and want it kept private. What do you sign?
qa.why: An NDA binds the other party to secrecy.

qa.q: A basic customer is offered the fuller plan at a higher price. What is that?
qa.why: An upsell offers a more expensive version.

qa.q: How many units must a business sell before income exactly covers its costs?
qa.why: At break-even there is neither profit nor loss.

qa.q: A person wants a move to another function without a rise in grade. What is it?
qa.why: A lateral move keeps the same level.

qa.q: A firm is wholly owned by another but trades under its own name. What is it?
qa.why: A subsidiary is a separate company controlled by a parent.

qa.q: Which statement best separates a shareholder from a stakeholder?
qa.right: A shareholder owns shares; a stakeholder is anyone affected by or able to influence the organisation
wrong: A stakeholder owns the company; a shareholder does not
A shareholder is an employee only
qa.why: Stakeholders include many groups beyond owners.

qa.q: A team's diary shows constant back-to-back meetings that overrun, leaving no recovery. What change helps?
qa.why: Buffer time absorbs overruns.

qa.q: A person is accountable for a result that the whole team produced. Which is true?
qa.right: They remain answerable even when others did the work
wrong: They are not answerable if they delegated
They share blame equally with everyone
They are answerable only for their own tasks
qa.why: Accountability stays with the person who owns the outcome.

qa.q: A customer was told the product would last two years, and it failed at four months. Which concept covers the repair?
qa.why: A warranty promises repair or replacement for faults.

qa.q: A job advert states a set number of hours at a stated hourly rate. What pay type is it?
qa.why: A wage is calculated per hour.
